Every input is\n// parsed at two sizes and the cost per byte compared: a linear parse keeps it\n// flat and a quadratic one multiplies it by the size ratio.\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\n\nimport { LinkNetwork } from '../src/index.js';\nimport { LINO_MAX_DEPTH, parseLinoCst } from '../src/lino-grammar.js';\n\n// The large input holds SIZE_RATIO times as many units as the small one.\nconst SIZE_RATIO = 8;\n// Linear parsing lands near 1, quadratic near SIZE_RATIO.\nconst MAX_PER_BYTE_GROWTH = 3;\nconst SAMPLES = 3;\nconst ATTEMPTS = 3;\n\nconst LINO_SCALING_CASES = [\n  { name: 'deep parentheses', units: 500, source: (n) => `${'('.repeat(n)}a${')'.repeat(n)}\\n` },\n  { name: 'unclosed groups', units: 500, source: (n) => `${'(a '.repeat(n)}\\n` },\n  {\n    name: 'deep indentation',\n    units: 500,\n    source: (n) => `${Array.from({ length: n }, (_, depth) => `${' '.repeat(depth % (LINO_MAX_DEPTH - 4))}a`).join('\\n')}\\n`,\n  },\n  { name: 'indented identifiers', units: 250, source: (n) => 'id:\\n  a\\n  b\\n    c\\n'.repeat(n) },\n  { name: 'long delimiter run', units: 2000, source: (n) => `${'\"'.repeat(n)}x${'\"'.repeat(n)}\\n` },\n  { name: 'unclosed quotes', units: 500, source: (n) => `${'\"a '.repeat(n)}\\n` },\n  { name: 'comments and groups', units: 250, source: (n) => 'a: b c # note\\n  child (x y)\\n'.repeat(n) },\n  { name: 'failing indented lines', units: 100, source: (n) => `x\\n${'  (broken\\n'.repeat(n)}` },\n];\n\n// The whole LiNo parse: the grammar CST and the links-notation semantics.\nfunction nanosPerByte(source) {\n  let best = Infinity;\n  for (let sample = 0; sample < SAMPLES; sample += 1) {\n    const started = process.hrtime.bigint();\n    const network = LinkNetwork.parse(source, 'LiNo');\n    best = Math.min(best, Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - started));\n    assert.equal(network.reconstructText(), source, 'the parse stays lossless');\n  }\n  return best / source.length;\n}\n\nfor (const { name, units, source } of LINO_SCALING_CASES) {\n  test(`the LiNo grammar reads ${name} without deep recursion and in linear time`, () => {\n    const small = source(units);\n    const large = source(units * SIZE_RATIO);\n    nanosPerByte(small); The npm `latest` dist-tag for\n  `meta-language` is 0.46.0, while crates.io and both package manifests in\n  this repository are at 0.58.2. RML's JavaScript range `^0.46.0` therefore\n  resolves to 0.46.0.\n- RML's facade tests in `js/tests/meta-language-support.test.mjs` (seven\n  tests) passed on meta-language 0.46.0 and also passed when pointed at this\n  branch's JavaScript sources through a scratch link. The second run is not a\n  clean installed artifact and does not satisfy any delivery or downstream\n  row. RML's Rust facade was not built against 0.58.2 during the audit.\n- RML parses with the label `RML`, which is not registered. Both runtimes\n  then fall back to the lossless text network; `rust/src/parser_registry.rs`\n  documents the fallback. A JavaScript probe during the audit returned a\n  Language link and one source token link per character, with no Syntax\n  links. The `LiNo` label gives the full Links Notation 0.22.0 CST.\n- RML's issue 181 records R4 (an RML dialect in the parser registry), R5 (all\n  manipulation through meta-language query and rewrite) and R6 (a strategy\n  library) as missing, and R1 to R3 as an overlay or partial.\n- RML filed meta-language issues 163, 165, 166, 171, 172 and 173. All were\n  closed at the audit date. Issue 171 asked for lockstep npm and crate\n  versions; the registries still differ.\n- RML pull request 184 adds one Links Notation front end\n  (`js/src/rml-lino-frontend.mjs`, `rust/src/lino_frontend.rs`) on\n  `links-notation` 0.20 and reported Links Notation issues 312 to 316: runtime\n  disagreement on lone carriage returns, Unicode spaces and singlets; lost\n  names on indented identifier lines; exponential nested groups and quadratic\n  time in Rust `parse_lino_to_links`; a Rust stack overflow with no 64-level\n  depth limit; and quadratic quote runs. All five were closed at the audit\n  date. meta-language's own Links Notation 0.22.0 grammar is tested against\n  these inputs (see the RML table), but RML does not use it.\n- formal-ai reported the quadratic `point_at_byte` (meta-language issue 193)\n  and the docs.rs build problem caused by `lindera` (meta-language issue 181);\n  both were closed. Its SQL and GraphQL semantic proposals are meta-language\n  issues 187 and 188, also closed.\n- formal-ai's `REQUIREMENTS.md` rows R347, R381, R1085-3 and R890-2 mention\n  meta-language. Row R526-3 uses \"meta-language\" for formal-ai's internal\n  meaning representation of natural language and does not refer to this\n  project.\n\n## What remains unverified\n\n- No workload of either consumer has been run against clean installed\n  meta-language artifacts. `I195-DOWNSTREAM-RML-WORKLOADS`,\n  `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-WORKLOADS` and\n  `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED` remain unverified.\n- `I195-DELIVERY-RML-CANDIDATE`, `I195-DELIVERY-RML-PUBLISHED`,\n  `I195-DELIVERY-NPM-PUBLISHED` and `I195-DELIVERY-CRATE-PUBLISHED` are not\n  shown by this document.\n- `I195-DOWNSTREAM-CONSUMER-MATRIX` asks for a check that fails when a row or\n  test named here does not exist. It does not say the consumer's own tests\n  pass on the current release.\n\n## Boundary with relative-meta-logic\n\nmeta-language does not take over RML's foundations or proof authority. RML's\nkernel, its many-valued and probabilistic semantics, its proof checking and\nits certified tactics stay in RML, as RML's requirement N6 states: soundness\nmust not be weakened and strategies must reuse the existing certified kernel\nsteps. meta-language supplies parsing, lossless representation, query,\nrewrite and translation machinery that RML may call. A proof result counts\nbecause RML's kernel accepts it, not because meta-language produced or\ntranslated it. The same applies to formal-ai: meta-language is a syntax and\ntranslation engine there and does not decide what formal-ai accepts as true.\n",

Reads all fragment files and determines the highest bump type\n   - Bumps the version in `Cargo.toml` accordingly\n   - Collects fragments into `CHANGELOG.md`\n   - Creates a git tag and GitHub release\n   - Do not select one convenient grammar, copy a generated parser, wrap an external engine, store a foreign grammar as a string, or rename imported files and call that the native implementation.\n- [ ] Imports/conversions are required authoring and interoperability tools (section 4), but their final product must be a full native grammar that meta-language itself can inspect, transform, execute and emit. Ordinary installed parsing must work without external grammar engines, subprocesses, foreign generated parsers/scanners, downloads or caller registration. Any generated acceleration must derive reproducibly from the native Links Notation definitions, not conceal another authoritative grammar.\n- [ ] Represent and implement the complete union of required grammar features: ordered/unordered alternatives, recursion including left recursion, precedence/associativity, ambiguity/conflicts, lexical priority and longest-match rules, Unicode/byte classes, token boundaries/trivia, lexer modes/channels/state, indentation/layout, context-sensitive predicates, semantic actions and attributes, captures/fields/aliases, parameterization, imports/inheritance, macros/notation, embedded languages, error/missing nodes and recovery. External scanner behavior and action semantics must become structured, executable link definitions, not uninterpreted source blobs or hidden language-specific callbacks.\n- [ ] Preserve every unique concept and semantic distinction. Follow imports, supporting lexer/scanner definitions and action code where necessary; importing only rule skeletons is incomplete. Fully automatic merging, concept recognition, deduplication and renaming\n\n- [ ] The default merge pipeline must be non-interactive and automatic: discover/import the inventoried grammar sources, recognize corresponding concepts even when names differ, reconcile their definitions, normalize names, deduplicate genuinely equivalent concepts, preserve unique concepts, and emit the canonical native grammar plus a reproducible provenance/decision report. A tool that just concatenates rules, prefixes every source namespace, or requires users to provide all correspondences does not satisfy this requirement.\n- [ ] Implement binding-aware concept/rule renaming throughout references, imports, captures, semantic actions, mappings and generated artifacts. Where explicit precedence between sources is needed, encode a reproducible rule justified by language specifications and independent evidence.\n- [ ] Define “best possible” with evidence: construct coverage and correctness first, preservation of unique features and shared reuse, then measured recovery quality, execution time and memory. The invariant\nenforced by the test suite is the same one used by the document fidelity\nmatrix: for every format and every entry in `GRAMMAR_CONSTRUCTS`, the construct\nis either represented without a lossy fallback or has exactly one documented\nfallback.\n\n## Per-format construct support\n\n| Construct | BNF |\n| --- | :---: |\n| empty-expression | ✅ |\n| sequence | ✅ |\n| ordered-choice | ⚠️ |\n| unordered-choice | ✅ |\n| optional-expression | ⚠️ |\n| zero-or-more-repetition | ⚠️ |\n| one-or-more-repetition | ⚠️ |\n| counted-repetition | ⚠️ |\n| character-range | ⚠️ |\n| character-class | ⚠️ |\n| any-character | ⚠️ |\n| terminal | ✅ |\n| case-insensitive-terminal | ⚠️ |\n| nonterminal | ✅ |\n| positive-predicate | ⚠️ |\n| negative-predicate | ⚠️ |\n| capture | ⚠️ |\n| atomic-rule | ⚠️ |\n| silent-rule | ⚠️ |\n| token-rule | ⚠️ |\n\n✅ lossless · ≈ equivalent spelling or normalization · ⚠️ documented lossy fallback\n\n## Documented lossy fallbacks\n\n| Format | Construct | Fallback |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| bnf | ordered-choice | emitted as an unordered BNF alternative; priority semantics are not preserved |\n| bnf | optional-expression | emitted through a synthetic helper production with an empty alternative |\n| bnf | zero-or-more-repetition | emitted through a recursive synthetic helper production with an empty alternative |\n| bnf | one-or-more-repetition | emitted through a recursive synthetic helper production plus one required item |\n| bnf | counted-repetition | emitted as required occurrences plus optional or recursive synthetic helper productions |\n| bnf | character-range | expanded to a synthetic helper production enumerating each character when the range is bounded |\n| bnf | character-class | expanded to a synthetic helper production for finite non-negated classes; unsupported classes are rejected |\n| bnf | any-character | unsupported by BNF emission and rejected instead of silently broadening the language |\n| bnf | case-insensitive-terminal | emitted as a case-sensitive literal and reported as lossy |\n| bnf | positive-predicate | unsupported by BNF emission and rejected because lookahead has no BNF equivalent |\n| bnf | negative-predicate | unsupported by BNF emission and rejected because lookahead has no BNF equivalent |\n| bnf | capture | emitted as the captured expression while dropping the capture label |\n| bnf | atomic-rule | emitted as a normal BNF production;
